properties.name: The unused Anchor node type is announced for removal: the retirement rule's first real entry, and the two hints that described a link nothing makes
properties.rationale:
WHY: Anthony's ruling on dec:anchor-retire-or-implement (accepted 2026-10-13): "Remove the unused Anchor type, but only after a rule for retiring things exists, because it would be the first thing ever taken off what Alex's MCP sees." The rule is req:the-mcp-server-keeps-working-as-is-and-door-improvements-are-additive-or-opt-in as amended on 2026-10-13, built as cap:a-served-item-is-removed-only-after-a-release-that-announced-it (#751): a DEPRECATING release in which the item still works, says it is going (for a schema item, in describe_schema) and the changelog carries a What to do line; then the NEXT release removes it. This is that rule's first real entry, and its deprecating half only. The decision stays accepted; it is carried out across two releases. The decision also asked whether a retired vocabulary item stops being offered or is offered with a warning; the rule answers it: offered with the mark for one release, then removed.

THE USAGE EVIDENCE that dec:a-tool-is-never-deleted-without-usage-evidence-across-projects-and-never-without-a-refusing-stub-first asks of a tool, applied to a node type: zero Anchors in all seven designs these MCP servers serve (counts in the summary). Designs outside them were not read, by instruction: no droplet store, and not Alex's, Seth's or Emily's designs. The deprecating release's notice is what protects those, and telling the people who rely on the MCP server is owed before it ships (flow:release-cut step 2). Who tells Alex, and how, is Anthony's open decision D3, which this change does not choose. The release carrying it must not ship until D3 is answered.

ONE ENTRY, NOT FOUR: design_intent and key_decisions are declared on no other type and leave with it; name, checksum and created_at stay declared on the types that share them; no edge type names Anchor as an endpoint (only `*` reaches it); and the surface check already lets a deprecated type take its properties with it. Property entries would only repeat the notice on every Anchor write.

THE WHAT-TO-DO WAS MEASURED, NOT COPIED: the decision's text says Snapshot generalizes Anchor ("temporal.rs:62 describes Snapshot as ..."), but the code puts that sentence on EpochType::Baseline (temporal.rs:225), DesignEpoch's hint says "Generalizes the P2→P3 Anchor", and add_epoch's `checksum` says "an Anchor is a checksummed baseline epoch". A Snapshot is one node's state at an epoch, written by snapshot_before_change. So the sentence names both tools. The decision's prose was left as written.

THE HINTS: on reflow2's design there are now 40 DriftEvents (the decision counted 37), and every one carries exactly one edge, DEPENDS_ON to an Artifact, as drift.rs write_drift_event draws it; fielded.rs draws it to the Environment and Release. Rewording a hint is not a removal: the surface record is untouched and no toolsnap moved.

THE LISTING FIX was found by the first real entry and is part of serving it correctly: describe_schema inserted `deprecations` before marking the whole reply, so the listed item, which holds a node_type, came back marked too. #751 is unreleased, so no client saw it.

req:intent-is-reinjected (dropped) is GOVERNED_BY the decision; this change changes nothing for it — the payload vocabulary it names (Snapshot, DesignEpoch, Decision, Constraint) stays, and only the type nothing reads goes.

WHAT REMOVAL WILL DO is measured, not built: fact:what-removing-the-anchor-type-does-to-a-graph-that-holds-one-measured-2026-10-14. A graph holding an Anchor is refused at open by the removal build, and its export is refused on import, contrary to the open refusal's own recipe; deleting the Anchor on 0.85.0 first is what works. TESTS FIRST: all four new tests failed on main at 959436d80 (4d8122650), and the changelog check failed without the fragment. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: DEPRECATES the Anchor node type in 0.85.0; the release after removes it, in a later PR. deprecation::REGISTRY (crates/reflow2-mcp/src/deprecation.rs, art:deprecation) gets its first real entry: Deprecation::node_type("Anchor", "0.85.0", "Nothing reads an Anchor; record a checksummed baseline with `add_epoch` (epoch_type `baseline`, with its `checksum`) and capture a node's state at it with `snapshot_before_change` (a Snapshot) instead.", "dec:anchor-retire-or-implement"). One entry for the type, none for its properties. THE TWO HINTS the decision says must move: DriftEvent's (schema/verify.yaml, art:schema-verify) no longer says it "References the Anchor it diverged from via DEPENDS_ON" and says it DEPENDS_ON the drifted Artifact, or a deployment drift's Environment and Release; Anchor's own (schema/structure.yaml, art:schema-structure) no longer says DriftEvents reference it and names the tools that do the job. describe_schema (tools/query.rs, art:tools-query) now lists `deprecations` after marking the reply, so a listed item is not itself marked. The comments of art:a-served-item-is-removed-only-after-a-release-that-announced-it-test no longer call the registry empty. NEW: art:the-unused-anchor-type-is-announced-for-removal-test implementing ver:the-unused-anchor-type-is-announced-for-removal (passing), which VERIFIES cap:a-served-item-is-removed-only-after-a-release-that-announced-it and is GOVERNED_BY the decision; and fact:what-removing-the-anchor-type-does-to-a-graph-that-holds-one-measured-2026-10-14 on the decision. A changelog.d fragment announces it under ### Deprecated with its What to do line. USAGE COUNTS, read-only scan_nodes node_type Anchor on 2026-10-14: 0 in child-reflow2 (reflow2), 0 in hub (its view covered the hub and its 6 members, each 0), 0 in flo2, 0 in reflow2-calculator, 0 in ifcopenshell-fork, 0 in agent-cad-engine, 0 in integrated-flo. NOT COUNTED: any design outside those servers, Alex's own local stores included. Nothing a client sends breaks: an Anchor is still created, read and exported; all 197 toolsnaps match; the surface check passes against v0.84.0's record, which this change does not touch.
